contract_F_answers.1_faithful_to_cited_formulation: yes at the level verifiable: tables, MRT basis, Eq. (4) including the B1 term, Eq. (18)'s 9/4, recoloring pair structure, secant wetting (lambda = 1/2, stop at n = 2), three-pass D3Q27 smoothing, the X_W 1D-Cartesian gradient and the seven-step ordering with site domains all match the sources read directly. Two items cannot be certified: the R5 coefficient mapping (correctly UNRESOLVED in section 4.2, wrongly CLOSED in section 11) and the phase convention (R-2)
contract_F_answers.2_current_vs_leclaire_differences: the MATHEMATICALLY_EQUIVALENT rows are the colour bookkeeping (A.1) and the polynomial equilibrium at alpha = W0 (A.5); the gradient stencil (A.7) is the same operator once the R5 caveat is attached. All other rows are real differences. The A.8 derivation (distribution-space perturbation vs moment-space injection) is the strongest analysis in the package: the deviatoric parts match under CapA <-> sigma, the isotropic parts differ in sign and magnitude by 3x, which no Laplace test can detect
contract_F_answers.3_followups_that_change_behaviour: explicit beta amplitude law (test 05: width 1.84 -> 1.12 monotone over beta 0.5 -> 1.0) and the unrelaxed post-collision perturbation (structural, A.8). The Akai closure is implemented but unmeasured, so it has no demonstrated effect
contract_F_answers.4_complex_wall_wetting: improves: under wetting_sign = -1 the same code reproduces 60 -> 51, 90 -> 83, 120 -> 113 deg (errors 7-9 deg), versus 55-73 deg errors at the default sign. The closure is likely correct and the convention is what is unresolved
contract_F_answers.5_conservation_corrections_to_retain: none as code (test 10 needs no overlay: 2.8e-13 per step total drift without one). Retain as practice the L17_CORE vs L17_PLUS_OVERLAY two-arm reporting and the solid-node-reservoir transient separation; keep every claim scoped to the f64 reference until a Taichi/f32 port repeats the audit
